2023

2023-01-11Test

Multiplex specific IgE and total IgE

Specific IgE measures sensitization. Clinical allergy requires concordant history. The report gives <0.3 kUA/L as negative. The introduction, cross-reactivity education and repeated displays of reactive allergens are separate from analyte results.

Confirmed infection and six-week recovery

Patient reports a positive SARS-CoV-2 test in May 2023, likely the third infection, with about six weeks of symptoms. Intermittent feverish or sick spells followed that summer.

Six-week infection followed by intermittent sick spells

Patient recalls a positive test in May and symptoms lasting six weeks, then brief feverish or sick spells with intervals of feeling normal over summer.

2023-09Milestone

Musty indoor air and air-conditioner fault with temporary throat symptoms

In September 2023, musty air and a malfunctioning air conditioner coincided with throat and breathing symptoms. Symptoms reportedly resolved following repairs. Mold exposure was suspected, not demonstrated as the cause.

2023-10 – 2023-12MilestoneDecline

Relapsing illness became persistent

Feverishness, sore throat, cognitive slowing and weakness recurred at roughly two-week intervals. A faint/partial positive test was reported. The third spell persisted, with severe cognitive dysfunction, panic, fragmented sleep and paresthesias. By December he required family help to return home.

2023-10 – 2023-11Baseline

Relapsing illness became persistently disabling

After two short illnesses separated by returns to usual activity, a third spell persisted. Patient described hours of profound cognitive shutdown, trouble operating a phone or opening a door, panic and fragmented sleep. In later chat he recalled being intermittently bedbound, then improving.

He recalled spending hours apparently unconscious in bed during the first month of illness, yet being able to walk between episodes. He also described panic attacks with a racing heart, sometimes waking him. Symptoms lessened over time while he was pacing and had introduced MCT oil.
S1:2098–2098
Recalled that the severe early crashes stopped from the day after he started MCT oil.
S1:2108–2108
Recalled no longer being intermittently bedbound over the same period.

2024-04-17MilestoneImprovement

NC protocol: rapid partial recovery after maraviroc

The patient retrospectively confirmed that the multi-ingredient NC protocol began on 17 April 2024. Reported components included B complex, DEKA, vitamin C, curcumin, CBD, cordyceps, ganoderma, shiitake, pectin, broccoli and antioxidants; one inulin/probiotic product started alongside the regimen. Fatigue and energy reportedly improved almost immediately to approximately the pre-maraviroc baseline, then plateaued. This was not a return to pre-illness health. Exact doses and individual component introduction dates remain uncertain.

2024-06-02 – 2024-10-20Baseline

Neurological/PENE variability leading up to NADH

The clinician identified the pre-NADH crashes as neurological PENE or brain-burning episodes. Pain could limit movement or speech. The diary also contains generic lack-of-strength ratings. The distinctive deep muscle fatigue and physical PEM first appeared after NADH. June 22 records about two hours unable to move or speak, September 22 about two hours barely able to move. Some days he could work productively.

Tracker history through October 20. This window includes the revised first exposure day. · Compared with Earlier function in the same tracker · The tracker dates the observations. The reviewer clarifies the treatment dates. S6 clarifies phenotype. Retrospective reports supply additional symptoms. Magnesium poisoning was a patient hypothesis. Exact dose and mechanism remain uncertain. S3:symptom:013 separately describes later CNS shutdown without muscle fatigue.

Q-NADH-PHENOTYPE
The clinician identified the pre-NADH crashes as neurological PENE or brain-burning episodes. Pain could limit movement or speech. The diary also contains generic lack-of-strength ratings. The distinctive deep muscle fatigue and physical PEM first appeared after NADH. The clinician identifies the October 23 “magnesium poisoning” entry as new deep muscle fatigue. The October 25 account describes progressive sleepiness and weakness, unusually good sleep, near-paralysis the next day, muscle cramps, and tingling without the usual pains. On November 2 the patient explicitly contrasted prior movement limitation during brain burning with fatigue now felt directly in the muscles, including when the brain burning was absent. S6 clarifies phenotype. Retrospective reports supply additional symptoms. Magnesium poisoning was a patient hypothesis. Exact dose and mechanism remain uncertain. S3:symptom:013 separately describes later CNS shutdown without muscle fatigue.

response:S5-R-V15-1
S5:313-313
Notes: Around 1, I took 10 mL Kender+ and possibly used BEMER before or afterward. A few hours later, around 4, I had terrible brain burning, dizziness and weakness. I hypothesized that THC had been synthesized from the hemp. This was the patient's hypothesis. The episode lasted two hours and I could not move or speak. A small amount of black stool in the morning and evening was attributed by the patient to alginite. Strong abdominal pain before the evening bowel movement resolved afterward. [V15]
Q-NADH-PHENOTYPE
The clinician identified the pre-NADH crashes as neurological PENE or brain-burning episodes. Pain could limit movement or speech. The diary also contains generic lack-of-strength ratings. The distinctive deep muscle fatigue and physical PEM first appeared after NADH. The clinician identifies the October 23 “magnesium poisoning” entry as new deep muscle fatigue. The October 25 account describes progressive sleepiness and weakness, unusually good sleep, near-paralysis the next day, muscle cramps, and tingling without the usual pains. On November 2 the patient explicitly contrasted prior movement limitation during brain burning with fatigue now felt directly in the muscles, including when the brain burning was absent. S6 clarifies phenotype. Retrospective reports supply additional symptoms. Magnesium poisoning was a patient hypothesis. Exact dose and mechanism remain uncertain. S3:symptom:013 separately describes later CNS shutdown without muscle fatigue.
10 mL around 1 was followed around 4 by severe brain burning, dizziness and weakness with inability to move or speak for two hours. The clinician identified the pre-NADH crashes as neurological PENE or brain-burning episodes. Pain could limit movement or speech. The diary also contains generic lack-of-strength ratings. The distinctive deep muscle fatigue and physical PEM first appeared after NADH.

Q-NADH-PHENOTYPE
The clinician identified the pre-NADH crashes as neurological PENE or brain-burning episodes. Pain could limit movement or speech. The diary also contains generic lack-of-strength ratings. The distinctive deep muscle fatigue and physical PEM first appeared after NADH. The clinician identifies the October 23 “magnesium poisoning” entry as new deep muscle fatigue. The October 25 account describes progressive sleepiness and weakness, unusually good sleep, near-paralysis the next day, muscle cramps, and tingling without the usual pains. On November 2 the patient explicitly contrasted prior movement limitation during brain burning with fatigue now felt directly in the muscles, including when the brain burning was absent. S6 clarifies phenotype. Retrospective reports supply additional symptoms. Magnesium poisoning was a patient hypothesis. Exact dose and mechanism remain uncertain. S3:symptom:013 separately describes later CNS shutdown without muscle fatigue.

Cool shower

After an early-evening cool shower, 15 minutes of well-being were followed by a sudden crash and severe brain fog for hours. The day had already been worse before the shower. The clinician identified the pre-NADH crashes as neurological PENE or brain-burning episodes. Pain could limit movement or speech. The diary also contains generic lack-of-strength ratings. The distinctive deep muscle fatigue and physical PEM first appeared after NADH.

Q-NADH-PHENOTYPE
The clinician identified the pre-NADH crashes as neurological PENE or brain-burning episodes. Pain could limit movement or speech. The diary also contains generic lack-of-strength ratings. The distinctive deep muscle fatigue and physical PEM first appeared after NADH. The clinician identifies the October 23 “magnesium poisoning” entry as new deep muscle fatigue. The October 25 account describes progressive sleepiness and weakness, unusually good sleep, near-paralysis the next day, muscle cramps, and tingling without the usual pains. On November 2 the patient explicitly contrasted prior movement limitation during brain burning with fatigue now felt directly in the muscles, including when the brain burning was absent. S6 clarifies phenotype. Retrospective reports supply additional symptoms. Magnesium poisoning was a patient hypothesis. Exact dose and mechanism remain uncertain. S3:symptom:013 separately describes later CNS shutdown without muscle fatigue.

reports:S4-R18
S4-R18
2024-10-20 – 2024-10-30MilestoneDecline

NADH-associated severe baseline decline and onset of physical PEM

During two NADH exposure periods (20–21 and 25–28 October 2024), the patient developed a previously unfamiliar, profound deep-muscle fatigue and physical post-exertional deterioration. A major crash was documented on 23 October; marked weakness and inability to get out of bed recurred on 29 October. The patient described a severe step down in functional baseline—from being able to leave home at times to frequently remaining in bed—and a new, persistent PEM and sensory-intolerance pattern. Neurological exertional exacerbations with brain burning had existed beforehand. There was partial improvement in November, but the subsequent baseline remained substantially impaired. The exposure is temporally associated with the decline; a sole cause cannot be established from these reports.

S1-M1617
The patient described severe neurological symptoms despite working with a clinical team. Gut symptoms had partly improved from constant pain and one bowel movement per week. Energy had improved, deep sleep had increased from about 20 minutes to 45–90 minutes, and testosterone had risen from the low end of the range. Brain fog and POTS persisted. He described a nonliposomal experimental nanocarrier formulation and relayed the developers’ claim that it could increase absorption of substances taken alongside it. He took a slightly larger than intended dose of the NADH formulation, then his usual magnesium dose about five hours later. He recalled a roughly 12-hour steady-state interval for the formulation. He became progressively sleepy and weak, slept unusually well, and felt effectively paralysed the next day. He had muscle cramps and tingling, without his usual pains and other symptoms. He called this magnesium toxicity but also considered an acute ME-related change. Symptoms began clearing as he drank large amounts of water. The team was considering a formulation intended to target the blood–brain barrier. He was considering switching to off-label trials if their experiments failed and was avoiding concurrent drugs because of the proposed absorption interaction.

oh and this time i felt it also when my brain wasn't burning, unlike before, so it seems to be independent now, whereas before i only had paralysis like events when my brain was "on fire" and more an action paralysis, and this time proper muscle fatigue

S3:symptom:013
* Post Exertional Malaise (PEM): * exertion causes sudden shutdown of executive function, both cognitive and physical * 1-3x/day, lasting a few hours, but sometimes recurring for days * but it’s never a continuous crash even then * progression: top of forearms/hands tingling (rapidly fluctuating, slightly corrosive, acid-like unpleasant sensation) → feet/calves tingling → nape tingling/pulsing → occipital lobe fatigue, pressures or sometimes headache → tranquilizing sensation and pulsing along spine → brain slows down suddenly (extreme CNS fatigue) → rarely almost full paralysis but usually just an intense malaise sensation (a bit like the flu), also tingling sometimes intensifies to a corrosion like pain → often narcoleptic sleep pressure, often fall asleep regardless of time of day * not muscle fatigue! * I can still move muscles, PEM seems to be in CNS with peripheral tingling as above, but if it’s very strong my “willpower” to move is zero * unless in severe crash, eating immediately lifts all symptoms (including sleep pressure), sometimes as soon as the first bite * Herxheimer reaction crashes are particularly violent, tingling is far more painful/corrosive * “evening PEM”: every day starting 5-6pm, getting at least initial parts of above progression (ie at least tingling) → IL-1beta circadian upregulation?

2024-10-23 – 2024-10-29Baseline

New post-NADH deep muscle fatigue and October decline

NADH was taken October 20–21 and restarted October 25–28, 2024, according to the reviewer. New deep muscle fatigue and a major crash were first documented October 23. Marked weakness and confinement to bed recurred October 29. The patient attributed a major baseline drop to NADH. November records describe partial recovery followed by a later relapse. Magnesium and exertion were also discussed. The clinician identifies the October 23 “magnesium poisoning” entry as new deep muscle fatigue. The October 25 account describes progressive sleepiness and weakness, unusually good sleep, near-paralysis the next day, muscle cramps, and tingling without the usual pains. On November 2 the patient explicitly contrasted prior movement limitation during brain burning with fatigue now felt directly in the muscles, including when the brain burning was absent. Daily overall ratings were 5/10 on October 21–22, 2/10 on October 23, and 3–4/10 through October 28. On October 29 he woke with numb or weak arms, especially around the shoulders and hands, and needed about an hour to get up. The clinician identifies this as the new deep muscle-fatigue phenotype. Later that day he felt tranquilized and confined to bed. Moving his limbs took considerable effort but remained possible. Muscle symptoms then eased and PENE followed. The diary also records suspected overexertion the previous evening.

The patient described severe neurological symptoms despite working with a clinical team. Gut symptoms had partly improved from constant pain and one bowel movement per week. Energy had improved, deep sleep had increased from about 20 minutes to 45–90 minutes, and testosterone had risen from the low end of the range. Brain fog and POTS persisted. He described a nonliposomal experimental nanocarrier formulation and relayed the developers’ claim that it could increase absorption of substances taken alongside it. He took a slightly larger than intended dose of the NADH formulation, then his usual magnesium dose about five hours later. He recalled a roughly 12-hour steady-state interval for the formulation. He became progressively sleepy and weak, slept unusually well, and felt effectively paralysed the next day. He had muscle cramps and tingling, without his usual pains and other symptoms. He called this magnesium toxicity but also considered an acute ME-related change. Symptoms began clearing as he drank large amounts of water. The team was considering a formulation intended to target the blood–brain barrier. He was considering switching to off-label trials if their experiments failed and was avoiding concurrent drugs because of the proposed absorption interaction. […]

S1-M1617
The patient described severe neurological symptoms despite working with a clinical team. Gut symptoms had partly improved from constant pain and one bowel movement per week. Energy had improved, deep sleep had increased from about 20 minutes to 45–90 minutes, and testosterone had risen from the low end of the range. Brain fog and POTS persisted. He described a nonliposomal experimental nanocarrier formulation and relayed the developers’ claim that it could increase absorption of substances taken alongside it. He took a slightly larger than intended dose of the NADH formulation, then his usual magnesium dose about five hours later. He recalled a roughly 12-hour steady-state interval for the formulation. He became progressively sleepy and weak, slept unusually well, and felt effectively paralysed the next day. He had muscle cramps and tingling, without his usual pains and other symptoms. He called this magnesium toxicity but also considered an acute ME-related change. Symptoms began clearing as he drank large amounts of water. The team was considering a formulation intended to target the blood–brain barrier. He was considering switching to off-label trials if their experiments failed and was avoiding concurrent drugs because of the proposed absorption interaction.

S3:symptom:013
* Post Exertional Malaise (PEM): * exertion causes sudden shutdown of executive function, both cognitive and physical * 1-3x/day, lasting a few hours, but sometimes recurring for days * but it’s never a continuous crash even then * progression: top of forearms/hands tingling (rapidly fluctuating, slightly corrosive, acid-like unpleasant sensation) → feet/calves tingling → nape tingling/pulsing → occipital lobe fatigue, pressures or sometimes headache → tranquilizing sensation and pulsing along spine → brain slows down suddenly (extreme CNS fatigue) → rarely almost full paralysis but usually just an intense malaise sensation (a bit like the flu), also tingling sometimes intensifies to a corrosion like pain → often narcoleptic sleep pressure, often fall asleep regardless of time of day * not muscle fatigue! * I can still move muscles, PEM seems to be in CNS with peripheral tingling as above, but if it’s very strong my “willpower” to move is zero * unless in severe crash, eating immediately lifts all symptoms (including sleep pressure), sometimes as soon as the first bite * Herxheimer reaction crashes are particularly violent, tingling is far more painful/corrosive * “evening PEM”: every day starting 5-6pm, getting at least initial parts of above progression (ie at least tingling) → IL-1beta circadian upregulation?
S1-M3753
today is worse. had a surprisingly okay day yesterday. think i spent too much time at my computer and have PENE today. not bedridden, so not as bad as a week back, but very brainfogged still.
S1-M4081
i'm doing better, no longer bedridden. i think taking the basic vitamins has helped recovery from my crash, suggesting your redox imbalance theory may be correct. i saw rapid baseline improvement after starting supplementing them (same day, these nano-carriers hit very fast).

Q-NADH-PHENOTYPE
The clinician identified the pre-NADH crashes as neurological PENE or brain-burning episodes. Pain could limit movement or speech. The diary also contains generic lack-of-strength ratings. The distinctive deep muscle fatigue and physical PEM first appeared after NADH. The clinician identifies the October 23 “magnesium poisoning” entry as new deep muscle fatigue. The October 25 account describes progressive sleepiness and weakness, unusually good sleep, near-paralysis the next day, muscle cramps, and tingling without the usual pains. On November 2 the patient explicitly contrasted prior movement limitation during brain burning with fatigue now felt directly in the muscles, including when the brain burning was absent. S6 clarifies phenotype. Retrospective reports supply additional symptoms. Magnesium poisoning was a patient hypothesis. Exact dose and mechanism remain uncertain. S3:symptom:013 separately describes later CNS shutdown without muscle fatigue.
2024-10-31 – 2024-11-02Baseline

Computer use followed by a two-hour near-paralysis-like crash

On November 2 he reported that sitting up to research and watch a series two days earlier preceded another two-hour episode. By the report he felt better but remained below his former level, resting all day. Cognitive exertion brought on symptoms sooner.

computer-induced attack reported Nov 2 as two days earlier · Compared with brief improvement at rest · The episode duration refers to near-paralysis. Rest after it was partly deliberate.

2024-11-09 – 2024-12-07Baseline

No longer bedridden; intermittent near-baseline mobility

By November 9 he was no longer bedridden, although still severely fogged. On November 12 he reiterated the mobility improvement and perceived benefit after resuming vitamins. On January 8 he recalled roughly two weeks bedridden, two weeks back at baseline without PEM, then another decline. A November 15 hospital trip provoked several hours of symptoms. On December 4 he felt roughly at his own baseline, and on December 7 could walk without dizziness while brain burning had subsided.

2024-12-08 – 2024-12-29Baseline

Very low threshold for visual and phone activity

On December 8 he woke with mild PEM, then had a one-to-two-hour evening crash. By December 17 an hour of motionless rest could be followed by another crash after five minutes on a phone, with neck, arm and forehead sensations and weakness. He clarified that the paralysis-like sensation could allow movement with great effort. On December 21 he sat in the living room for several morning hours, then crashed. At month end he described relief in darkness without visual stimulation.

Dec 8 symptoms reported Dec 9; further decline documented Dec 17; later symptoms observed Dec 29 · Compared with earlier December functioning · Patient suspected recent blood sampling added to an already developing decline. Severity across the entire month was variable.

The patient reported one episode of marked sympathetic overactivation during several quarter-patch uses, when the NC cocktail was taken nearby. Spaced uses felt different. A later patch was suspected in solar-plexus and left-sided spasms, which eased after L-theanine. A one-third patch felt more noticeable than one-quarter.

2025-04-08MilestoneImprovement

Ivabradine: reduction in resting and standing heart rate

Ivabradine 5 mg twice daily was started around 8–9 April 2025 for orthostatic tachycardia. The patient reported a lower standing heart rate by 9 April (at one point approximately 90 bpm) and about 10 bpm lower heart rate on 10 April. A later retrospective account estimated reductions of about 10 bpm at rest and 15–20 bpm standing. This was a modest heart-rate benefit; no clear improvement in the broader illness was reported. Treatment was temporarily interrupted in April, then restarted on 23 April; subsequent uninterrupted exposure cannot be established from these records.

2025-05-19 – 2025-06-08Baseline

Variable cognitive tolerance and limited daily walking

A poisoned crash cluster around May 19 overlapped with a new mixture and exertion. He later described a day of drawing without the usual PEM. A house move exceeded his activity budget; on June 8 he estimated 500–1,000 steps daily and said short walks could be tolerated.

May mixture dates disputed by a day; June 8 explicit report · Compared with post-hospital state · This is a mobility estimate for June, not a permanent daily step count. The drawing report describes a single better activity window.

2025-06-21MilestoneDecline

Recurrent severe crashes after a single rapamycin dose

A single 0.5 mg rapamycin dose on 21 June 2025 was followed by a sequence of severe CNS and upper-body fatigue episodes and crashes over approximately ten days. This represents recurrent episodes after one administration, not repeated dosing or one continuous ten-day attack. The temporal association does not establish causation.

2025-06-21 – 2025-06-30Baseline

Repeated profound fatigue and sleep-pressure attacks

Following one reported rapamycin dose, very intense afternoon crashes recurred over about ten days, including severe CNS/upper-body fatigue, corrosive tingling, inability to speak during worse attacks and renewed head burning/pressures. On June 26 he reported extreme sleepiness on four of five days.

dosing and indexed diary observations; recalled duration approximate · Compared with earlier fluctuating pattern with better mornings · This spans intermittent attacks, not uninterrupted immobility. Tea/other changes, background PEM and variable activity overlapped; recovery of the pre-trial baseline is not demonstrated here.

2025-07 – 2025-09Milestone

Green stools and GI disturbance following July treatment changes

Green stool appeared shortly after ensitrelvir began on 1 July 2025. Further episodes of green diarrhea, abdominal symptoms and systemic tingling developed amid overlapping trials of Gou teng, SuperHMO and changes in diet. Attribution to ensitrelvir remains uncertain, particularly given the preceding rapamycin-associated deterioration and several overlapping interventions. A restricted, low-fat diet and later GI improvement were documented. The patient retrospectively suspected that PEA/luteolin and the concurrent GI-stabilization/dietary regimen contributed to improving the green stools; multiple interventions overlapped, so that response is not attributable to one product.

Recurrent systemic flares and reduced speech tolerance

Tingling and green diarrhea recurred during overlapping gou teng, SuperHMO and other exposures. He worried about a new fatigue phenotype. July 27 he could communicate using brief yes/no questions but had difficulty speaking at length and tracking conversation. July 31 a violent crash followed both recent activity and xylitol intake.

End-of-July GI symptoms and PEM

Reports bloating, itching and shortness of breath responding to H1/H2 drugs, then repeated severe crashes, tremors, disorientation and sleep in a week with xylitol exposure, SLU-PP-332 pause and several other changes.

2025-07-30Response

H1/H2 blockers / xylitol-containing meals

Itch improved in roughly 40 minutes after H1/H2 blockers during bloating and dyspnea. Later crash occurred despite no clear bloating or histamine symptoms.

2025-08-19 – 2025-09-04Milestone

Liver and pancreatic enzymes normalized after earlier elevations

Following the green-stool and abdominal-symptom period, repeat testing on 4 September 2025 showed normalization of the previously elevated ALT, amylase and lipase: ALT 80 → 40 U/L, amylase 113 → 62 U/L and lipase 156 → 25 U/L between 19 August and 4 September. AST was at the laboratory upper limit (50 U/L) on 19 August and fell to 29 U/L. The patient suspected that a contemporaneous GI-stabilization regimen, possibly including PEA/luteolin, helped the green-stool symptoms. This temporal overlap does not establish that the regimen normalized the enzymes or caused the prior abnormalities.

2025-09-01Milestone

Amatica blood draw and subsequent research-test results

A mobile nurse completed the Amatica blood draw at approximately 06:00 on 1 September 2025. The patient described being fasting and experiencing hunger-related tingling before collection. Partial research-panel results were received on 1 October, with a second batch on 15 October; the supplied laboratory report is dated 20 November 2025. RNA-seq results were reported available on 14 March 2026, but the RNA export does not confirm that its sample was collected on 1 September. Research ranges and gene-expression findings are exploratory, not validated diagnoses.

2025-11 – 2025-12MilestoneDecline

Wrist-fatigue onset and change in nape/forehead pattern

A spore probiotic was tried November 18 onward and restarted November 26; a single bezisterim dose followed on December 1. The new wrist-specific fatigue pattern was retrospectively dated to this period. Nape fatigue had been reported by February 5, 2025, and a different deep muscle-fatigue episode occurred after NADH in October 2024; the late-2025 nape syndrome was described as more prominent. Behind-eye and lactate-like forehead symptoms and a lower functional threshold were also reported. Either treatment, other exposures or disease fluctuation may contribute; the cause is unresolved.

2025-11-04 – 2025-11-21Baseline

More laptop tolerance with dimming, red filter and pacing

Despite occasional crashes he described being at his usual baseline on November 4. By November 21 he reported managing a dimmed/red laptop through the day by pacing passive media and some chatting. He contrasted this with immediate PEM from turning over in bed at the earlier winter nadir.

Nov 4 day and Nov 21 description of usual functioning · Compared with preceding winter most severely impaired state · Adaptive equipment and task selection changed what he could tolerate. This does not establish comparable capacity for work, ordinary screens or unpaced activity.

2025-12-01 – 2025-12-19Baseline

New persistent nape/wrist and forehead symptoms with a lower threshold

Fatigue and intermittent head symptoms preceded the bezisterim dose. Marked CNS fatigue followed the next day amid concurrent probiotic and meals. By December 5 nape symptoms were nearly continuous. On December 16 standing to go to the toilet provoked symptoms even outside a perceived crash. By December 19 he was emerging from the deepest crash but felt below his former level.

diary dates and contemporaneous reports · Compared with pre-trial screen and activity tolerance · The patient explicitly questioned whether bezisterim, the spore probiotic, or an overlap explained the change. Subsequent state is a different question from causality.

2026-03-08 – 2026-03-26Baseline

Severe Redaxin-period crash followed by reported recovery of the earlier baseline

Following one relatively better day he described a severe crash with suicidal distress around the initial Redaxin trial. March 18 he thought he had recovered the level preceding the SAG/post-sexual cluster. By March 26 he described his usual daytime tingling, evening PEM and post-sexual poisoned crashes.

2026-05-18 – 2026-06-20Baseline

Flares around multiple small trials and cognitive exertion

Timed diary entries describe nape, wrist and CNS fatigue and sleep pressure around typing, reading, and trials including injected B12. By June he described similar troubling reactions across several trials and severe distress about persistent disability.

S1:76176–76182
The patient said they had lost hope of recovery after similar adverse reactions to B12, lithium, KL-1333, ASHA and imidazenil. They described intending to end their life later that year after putting affairs in order and wrote a farewell. No subsequent action is established by this message. He reported similar adverse responses during recent trials of B12, lithium, KL, ASHA and IMI. He described severe hopelessness about recovery and future suicidal intent at that time. […]

2026-06 – 2026-11Milestone

Hepatitis C antiviral courses: Ledifos, Velpanat and Darvoni

Ledifos, Velpanat and Darvoni were taken in separate courses with interruptions and switches. One Velpanat exposure was followed by rapid brain discomfort, a severe crash and sleep, prompting a pause. The patient subsequently completed approximately two months of Darvoni and reported that Velpanat was tolerated when resumed after Darvoni ran out. Responses varied by period; the initial adverse episode did not mean every later Velpanat dose was intolerable.

2026-07-08 – 2026-07-25Baseline

Recurrent internal torso tremor interfered with sleep

The patient described evening chest/solar-plexus hammering after an intense episode and subsequent stress; as little as about three hours sleep on some nights. Overexertion intensified the symptom. On July 25 he reported roughly one music track of the referenced length before burning and fatigue.

Q-S5-NADH-START
The reviewer specifies October 20–21 and October 25–28, 2024, inclusive. The tracker records an evening start October 21 and recalls a dose October 22. The retrospective history gives later dates. These accounts disagree on exposure timing. Previous reconstruction: The S5 calendar diary dates NADH initiation to the evening of October 21, 2024, excess NADH to October 22, and the first documented physical crash to October 23. Magnesium followed NADH by about five hours. The exact onset across the night of October 22–23 is unresolved. S6 clarifies phenotype. Retrospective reports supply additional symptoms. Magnesium poisoning was a patient hypothesis. Exact dose and mechanism remain uncertain. S3:symptom:013 separately describes later CNS shutdown without muscle fatigue. S5 does not name a restart. S1-M1899 supports an inferred October 25 night restart. The later S3 account places it October 28–29. An October 23 all-lipo hold does not specify NADH.
* NADH * developed PEM from it, had a massive crash only after 3 days of supplementing (never had such a crash before) * likely due to upset NAD+/NADH balance and uncovering existing complex I dysfunction
